- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent prices are falling sharply.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — if sentiment flips from negative to positive, forecast should not immediately spike; allow 2–3 days of lag before adjusting.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply downward correction by 5–10% of the spike magnitude.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish” sentiment followed by price collapse, model tends to overcorrect; anticipate downward drift and adjust forecast downward 1–3% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 5 days are significantly above true outcome, apply a “soft reset” — reduce first 3 days by 2–5% to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.
